---
title: "Course preparations"
---

Please prepare these three things before the workshop, so we can start using Git right away:

1. Install Git
2. Create a GitHub account
3. Install GitHub Desktop and sign in

# Install Git on your machine

Below are short instructions for each operating system (see also the [official guides](https://git-scm.com/downloads)).
If you already have Git installed, please [update it](https://www.howtogeek.com/759319/how-to-check-and-update-your-git-version/) to a recent version.

:::{.panel-tabset}

# Windows

[Download Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) ("Click here to download") and install it with the default settings.

This also installs **Git Bash**, a terminal for Git. Open it (search for "Git Bash" in the Windows search bar) and run:

```sh
git --version
```

If you see a version number, the installation worked.

# Linux (Ubuntu)

Install Git from the terminal:

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install git
```

Check the installation with:

```sh
git --version
```

# macOS

Open the Terminal app and run:

```sh
git --version
```

If Git is already installed, you will see a version number.

If not, macOS will ask you to install the "command line developer tools". Click **Install**, wait until it's finished and run `git --version` again.

Alternatively, if you use [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/), you can install Git with:

```sh
brew install git
```

:::

# Sign up for GitHub

We use GitHub as remote repository in the workshop. [Create an account here](https://github.com/join).

::: {.callout-tip}

## Free benefits for students and academic staff

Students and academic staff can get free benefits through [GitHub Education](https://github.com/education), e.g. GitHub Pro for students or free GitHub Copilot.
You need to apply and verify your affiliation (e.g. with a student ID or enrollment certificate, i.e. "Immatrikulationsbescheinigung").
You don't need this for the workshop, but it might be interesting if you use GitHub long-term.

:::

# Install GitHub Desktop

In the workshop, we use GitHub Desktop to work with Git.
Follow Part 1 (Installing GitHub Desktop) and Part 2 (Configuring your account) of [this guide](https://docs.github.com/en/desktop/installing-and-configuring-github-desktop/installing-and-authenticating-to-github-desktop/setting-up-github-desktop#part-1-installing-github-desktop).

When GitHub Desktop asks you to **configure Git**, use your name and the email address of your GitHub account. This is shown on all your commits.
You can change it later under **File -> Options -> Git** (macOS: **GitHub Desktop -> Settings -> Git**). This setting is also used by Git in the terminal, RStudio or VS Code.

:::{.callout-note}

## Linux users

There is no official GitHub Desktop for Linux, but you can install the community version from [shiftkey/desktop](https://github.com/shiftkey/desktop). Then continue with Part 2 of the guide above.

:::
